newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban says Dostum's forces now fighting.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban says Dostum's forces now fighting.

text.p: The forces of Afghanistan's powerful Uzbek chief General Abdul Rashid Dostum are now fighting the Taleban Islamic movement in support of the ousted government forces, a Taleban spokesman said on Thursday.

A Pakistan-based Afghan news service quoted Taleban acting Information Minister Amir Khan Mutaqi as saying about 50 fighters of the joint forces of Dostum and ousted government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood were killed in fighting on Wednesday north of the Taleban-held capital Kabul.

Dostum's Jumbish-i-Milli movement has entered into an alliance with Masood's Jamiat-i-Islami but Mutaqi had said in Kabul on Wednesday it was not yet clear whether the Jumbish forces were involved in the fighting.
But the Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted Mutaqi as saying in an interview on Thursday that Dostum's forces "have openly taken part in the offensives" against Taleban north of Kabul.
Those killed included a general whose documents showed that he belonged to Dostum's forces, AIP quoted Mutaqi as saying.
He said Dostum's forces had not only taken part in the fighting at Jabal os-Siraj and Charikar towns, which Masood's forceshe Taleban, but also taken part in "looting" the local population.
The Taleban took Kabul at the end of last month, and now have control of about two-thirds of the country.
